cards.text: Isaiah son of Amoz, a prophet, receives a burden against Babylon, a great city. Pull up a stool by the oven, friend, and lean in.

It opens with a signal: raise a banner on a barren hilltop, call out and wave your hand, so they can enter the gates of the nobles. That's a LOT of waving for somebody Isaiah hasn't even named yet, and friend, I wave with a mustache.

cards.question: A banner goes up on a bare hilltop. Then the burden says, "I have commanded My sanctified ones…" Who else does it say are summoned?
In the burden, the warriors are summoned to execute My ___ and exult in My triumph.

cards.text: Listen: a tumult on the mountains like a great multitude, and an uproar among the kingdoms like nations gathered together. That's LOUDER than the dead batteries I shared a drawer with, arguing over who had the most charge left.

cards.question: There's an uproar on the mountains and among the kingdoms. What does Isaiah say is going on?

answers.text: The LORD of Hosts raising an army
The kings of Egypt making a treaty
The tribes of Israel coming home

cards.text: This army is coming from faraway lands, from the ends of the heavens. The LORD and the weapons of His wrath are on the move.

cards.question: The LORD and the weapons of His wrath are coming to destroy the whole ___.
Then the cry goes out to wail. What reason does Isaiah give?

answers.text: The Day of the LORD is near
The king of Babylon has died

cards.text: The Day of the LORD will come as destruction from the Almighty, and all hands will fall limp.

cards.question: On the Day of the LORD, every man's heart will ___.

cards.text: Terror, pain and anguish will seize the people. They'll look at one another, their faces flushed with fear.

cards.question: With terror and anguish seizing them on the Day of the LORD, Isaiah says the people will writhe like someone. Who?

cards.text: Behold, the Day of the LORD is coming, cruel, with fury and burning anger. It's coming to make the earth a desolation.

cards.question: Isaiah says the Day of the LORD is coming to destroy the sinners within the earth.

cards.text: The stars of heaven and their constellations won't give their light, and the rising sun will be darkened. Friend, my whole sky lights up one cookie box at a time, so that one hits me right in the apron.

cards.question: On the Day of the LORD, Isaiah says the moon will still give its light.

cards.text: Then the burden goes on: "I will punish the world for its evil and the wicked for their iniquity."

cards.question: The burden says the wicked will be punished. Who else does it say will be brought low?

cards.text: Next comes gold, even the gold of Ophir. And as a guy who once sold for 25 cents, I am NOT the expert on precious things.

cards.question: The burden says man will be made scarcer than pure gold, rarer than the gold of Ophir. What's that picture saying?

answers.text: Very few people will be left
Gold will run out in the land

cards.text: The heavens will tremble, and the earth will be shaken from its place at the wrath of the LORD of Hosts. And everyone will scatter like a hunted gazelle, like a sheep without a shepherd.

cards.question: Scattered like a sheep without a shepherd, each person will return to his own ___.

cards.text: Whoever is caught will be stabbed, and whoever is captured will die by the sword. Their infants will be dashed to pieces before their eyes, their houses will be looted, and their wives will be ravished.
Then the burden names who's coming, the Medes, a people from the land of Media: "Behold, I will stir up against them the Medes…"

cards.question: The Medes who will be stirred up against them have a great desire for silver and gold.

cards.text: Their bows will dash young men to pieces, with no mercy on the fruit of the womb and no pity on the children. And Babylon, the jewel of the kingdoms, the glory of the pride of the Chaldeans, Babylon's people, will be overthrown.

cards.question: Isaiah says Babylon will be overthrown by God like two other cities. Which two?
Isaiah says that after Babylon is overthrown, she will never be inhabited again.

cards.text: Not even a nomad will pitch his tent there, and no shepherd will rest his flock there.

cards.question: Isaiah says that once Babylon is empty, new residents will move in. Who will live there?

cards.text: Hyenas will howl in her fortresses, and jackals in her luxurious palaces. The jewel of the kingdoms is headed for the WORST rental listing you have ever seen.

cards.question: Isaiah ends with one more word about Babylon's time. He says her days will be prolonged for many years yet.
